own_solution.law: Bernoulli + continuity for a horizontal Venturi with differential manometer
assumptions: manometer lines filled with flowing liquid

T2A08.regime: wide-section pressure well above the pressure drop so the throat stays above vapour pressure (no cavitation)

T6339.regime: wide-section pressure well above the pressure drop (no cavitation)

defect_reasons.other: The K regime 'q > dp' only keeps the throat pressure positive, not above the liquid's vapour pressure (the true cavitation bound), and the out-of-regime reference expression substitutes q for dp, which is not the physics of a cavitating Venturi; all listed values (170-350 kPa vs dp = 14.8 kPa) are far inside any sensible regime, so no certified answer is affected.

notes: Verified: dp = 14817.6 Pa, Q = 11.0395 L/s; rho_m = 1590 -> 2.38885, 2500 -> 3.80898, 3100 -> 4.50684 L/s (all checked by hand). In pass 1 I classed the absolute pressure as C; the authors' K (cavitation regime) is also defensible and the invariance holds either way. Height of axis C (z cancels for horizontal pipe) agrees. Barometer and earlier-experiment sentences D correct; minimal pairs T2C4F/T3597 and T6113/T609E share 2500 kg/m^3; T90FF/T5A70 are declared numeral-free controls.
